segments.text: Welcome to the Athar Open Agentic Pact, a community proposal from ODA and AIREV. This guided narration walks you through the pact, its community model, six pillars, governance, impact tiers, and the Athar OS roadmap. Use the arrows to move at your own pace.

segments.slideScript: Welcome to the Athar Open Agentic Pact — a community proposal by the Office of Development Affairs and AIREV. Build once. Run everywhere. Lift everyone. Over the next thirty-nine slides we set out the agreement, the community, the six pillars, the actors, the roadmap, the impact tiers and Athar OS.

segments.text: Section one, the Pact. The Athar Open Agentic Pact is an open commitment between institutions, partners and platforms to learn, build and deploy agentic AI for public benefit. It is a community proposal from ODA and AI Rev, designed as a community, not a product. Signatories agree on shared standards, an open plugin approach and measurable real-world outcomes.
segments.source: textToSpeech call of the orchestrated run (step 6–8), generated 2026-09-30T06:03Z; audio copied from the platform media URL, not re-synthesised
segments.slideScript: One open pact for agentic AI that serves people. Athar joins institutions, builders and learners around a single, published standard, so an agent built in one place can be trusted, reused and measured everywhere. The promise is simple: agentic AI that leaves a lasting, verifiable trace in people's lives.

segments.source: textToSpeech call of the orchestrated run (step 6–8), generated 2026-09-30T06:03Z; audio copied from the platform media URL, not re-synthesised
segments.slideScript: Why a pact, and not just a product launch? Because tools alone do not change outcomes. A pact commits every signatory to shared rules, open interfaces and independent measurement. It turns scattered pilots into a coordinated programme with named owners, agreed baselines and results that can be audited.

segments.text: Section two, the Community Model. Every webinar, chapter event and challenge should lead somewhere real, so the model is built around four outcomes for every participant. Learn agentic AI, build a useful agent through the Builder Journey and Marketplace, deploy it through a named Accountable Institution, and measure a real-world benefit with baseline evidence of time saved, better service, or wider reach.
segments.source: textToSpeech call of the orchestrated run (step 6–8), generated 2026-09-30T06:05:09Z; audio copied from the platform media URL, not re-synthesised
segments.slideScript: Section two: the community model. Every webinar, chapter event and challenge should lead somewhere specific and real. So the model is built around four outcomes for every participant. One: learn agentic AI, building a practical understanding of agents, prompting, verification and responsible use. Two: build a useful agent, moving from an idea to a validated agent through the builder journey and the marketplace. Three: deploy through an institution, putting that agent to work inside a named, accountable deployment. And four: measure a real-world benefit, with baseline and outcome evidence of time saved, better service or wider reach.

segments.slideScript: Section seven: impact and funding. Impact is measured in three tiers, from learning, to deployed agents, to real-world benefit. The pact proposal of the twenty-fourth of September and the impact-tiers paper set the baseline now, with gating items such as the licence field and open-book fees resolved first.
